title: Legal Aspects in Hospitality and Tourism: Main Exam, 13 December 2018
school: School of Hospitality, Travel and Tourism Management

unitTitle: Legal Aspects in Hospitality and Tourism
instructions: ANSWER QUESTION ONE IN SECTION A AND ANY OTHER TWO QUESTIONS IN SECTION B.

parts.text: Outline any four reasons of legislation in a country.
Distinguish between primary and secondary legislation.
Using an illustration describe the structure of courts in Kenya.
Using Donoghue versus Stevenson's principles explain how restaurateur's can guard against torts of negligence in a contract for the role of food and drinks.
Identify five types of liquour licences.
The cost to pursue or defend a law suit can be very high. In civil cases a number of alternatives are available known as alternative dispute resolution (ADR) examine three methods of ADR.
Discuss two types of covenants applied in leasehold agreements.
Explain any five restrictions to absolute control in freehold ownership.

items.text: Analyze any five essential elements required for a booking contract to be enforceable in a court of law.

parts.text: Identify five restrictions to the duty of care spelt out by occupiers liability act.
Explain the obligations of employees at work.

items.text: A guest was demed a room because the hotel was overbooked. In this case the guest was entitled to compensatory damages. (i) Define the term compensatory damages giving two relevant examples. (ii) Establish measures you would take as a manager to avoid a potential law suit. (iii) Examine the duties of an inner keeper.
